move: testimonial stack fans out, each card lifts front then tucks, collapses
how: Four white testimonial cards sit in a tight offset stack (y -6 and scale -0.03 per depth) over a blurred photo. At 2.5% they fan out to rotations of -21, -7, 7 and 21deg around a low pivot (transform-origin 50% 150%, expo.out 0.7s, 40ms stagger). From 21% each card in turn lifts to the front (rotation 0, y -26, scale 1.06, expo.out 0.42s, zIndex 10), holds, then tucks back to its fan angle +4deg at scale 0.98 (power2.inOut 0.36s) and settles; the dot row tracks the active card. Cards are 0.72s apart. At 91% the fan collapses back into the stack (expo.inOut 0.5s, 30ms stagger) and z-indexes are restored.
adapt: Replace the four quotes, names, roles and avatar gradients and the label; card count drives the fan angles (14deg per card). Keep the 0.42s expo.out lift, 0.36s tuck and 0.72s cadence.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the blurred bg, label, deck of cards and dots inside el and applies the initial stack with gsap.set. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with step = 0.18*D and start = 0.21*D; zIndex swaps are .set() calls on the timeline.
caveats: the collapse (starting at 3.63s + 0.5s) overruns the 4s register duration slightly, so the final frame is not quite the tight stack
the last dot stays active at the end while frame 0 highlights the first
filter: blur(10px) on a full-frame background image
